newsitem.title: USA: Israel's Sharansky defends Jerusalem groundbreaking.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Sharansky defends Jerusalem groundbreaking.

text.p: Israeli cabinet minister Natan Sharansky on Tuesday defended his government's decision to break ground on a controversial Jewish housing project, saying it was an essential step in the peace process.

Sharansky said Israel needed to begin construction on the housing project in predominantly Arab East Jerusalem as a politically logical next step for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to shore up domestic support.

"For Israel to continue building in Jerusalem is a very important, necessary integral part of the continuation of the peace process in the Middle East," Sharansky told reporters at the National Press Club.

He said any halt in the housing project construction, which he said was agreed to under the previous Israeli government and on which there was a broad domestic consensus, would jeopardise support for the peace process.
Sharansky, now Israel's minister of commerce and industry, was well known as an imprisoned dissident in the former Soviet Union.
